findings.fix: the maximum available friction between A and B is only μ₁mg = (1/4)mg, where μ₁ = 1/4 is the block-plank coefficient (below, μ₂ = 1/2 is the road-plank coefficient and M = 2m is the plank mass)

notes: Answer agrees on all parts. Required common-deceleration friction on A is m(g/2) = 0.5mg > 0.25mg available, so they slip; a_A = g/4, a_B = (3mg/2 - mg/4)/(2m) = 5g/8; relative 3g/8 from zero relative speed gives t^2 = 16l/(3g); the displacements follow and differ by exactly l. The result assumes the plank is still moving at that time (t < 8v/(5g)), which the question implies; the second common-mistake entry's number (4 sqrt(l/5g)) follows from its stated cause.
